name: CO2 to methanol and fuels
principle: CO2 from a point source and electrolytic hydrogen are reacted over a catalyst to make methanol. Carbon Recycling International's George Olah plant at Svartsengi, Iceland uses geothermal power plant flue-gas CO2 and electrolysis hydrogen, was commissioned in 2012 and was scaled from 1,300 to 4,000 t/yr.

source.note: Carbon Recycling International, George Olah plant page

costs.metric: e-methanol production cost, CO2 from combined renewable sources, 2015-2018 estimate
costs.basis: IRENA 'where we should be' assumptions; green H2 4,000-8,000 USD/t and CO2 10-50 USD/t; falls to 410-750 by 2030 and 250-630 by 2050 (no carbon credit)

source.note: IRENA/Methanol Institute Innovation Outlook: Renewable Methanol (January 2021), Table: Estimated costs of renewable methanol up to 2050, p. 82, read 2026-11-11

costs.metric: e-methanol production cost, CO2 from DAC only, 2015-2018 estimate
costs.basis: DAC CO2 300-600 USD/t; falls to 600-1,070 by 2030 and 290-630 by 2050 (no carbon credit); a USD 50/t CO2 credit lowers cost about USD 80/t MeOH

source.note: IRENA/Methanol Institute Innovation Outlook: Renewable Methanol (January 2021), Estimated-costs table, p. 82, read 2026-11-11

costs.metric: bio-methanol total production cost, biomass feedstock below USD 6/GJ
costs.basis: 327-561 USD/t from biomass, 414-583 USD/t from MSW; at USD 6-15/GJ feedstock rises to 447-714 (biomass) and 556-764 (MSW)

source.note: IRENA/Methanol Institute Innovation Outlook: Renewable Methanol (January 2021), Total production cost table, p. 71, read 2026-11-11
